title: Self-Control
definition: Self-Control is Spirit-enabled restraint and disciplined obedience in desires, words, habits, and actions.
summary: Self-Control is Spirit-enabled mastery over desires, impulses, habits, and reactions under the lordship of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives freedom from slavery to sin and forms disciplined holiness in His people by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Self-control is Spirit-formed restraint and wise ordering of desires under the lordship of Christ. Scripture treats self-control as a fruit of the Spirit and a necessary part of faithful discipleship.

Self-control is not mere willpower or personality strength. It is grace training the believer to say no to destructive desires and yes to what honors God.

Jesus lived in perfect obedience and resisted temptation. His Spirit enables believers to fight impulses, appetites, words, and habits that would master them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Uncontrolled desire can damage souls, families, bodies, finances, witness, and worship. Self-control gives hope that believers are not helpless before every appetite or impulse.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name the desire that most often tries to rule you. Build practical boundaries, seek accountability, pray before temptation becomes action, and rely on the Spirit rather than pride in your willpower.
